Hi Sarah / Alex 

Thanks again for taking the time to join the demo this morning. Appreciate the detailed questions on latency and streaming  great conversation. Attached is a concise SLO checklist that summarizes the performance targets we discussed and the data we'll need for a tight POC. High-level recap: 

- Demo highlights: streaming responses with token-level flush, stable p95 latency at ~110ms on our Dedicated 8xA100 config for the sample workload you shared.
- Key outstanding items: concurrency target (you mentioned up to 200 concurrent sessions), burst throughput requirements, and whether strict p50 vs p95 targets are the decision criteria.
- Next steps I propose (MAP):
  1) Share production-ish sample workload (payload sizes + expected session concurrency)  you
  2) Schedule a 90-min technical workshop with Rishi to validate streaming and KV-cache behavior  week of 5/25
  3) Agree on SLOs for POC (latency p95 target, throughput baseline, allowed error-rate)

I've attached the SLO_Checklist.xlsx and a short MAP_Draft.pdf (stub) to help structure the POC. If you can confirm the concurrency envelope and whether streaming token-level latency is a hard requirement (vs aggregate response latency), we can finalize the resource recommendations.

From: Alex Reed <alex@fintechco.com>

Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FintechCo performance recap & SLO checklist

Thanks Marissa  good summary. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

1) Concurrency: Our goal for the initial POC is to validate up to 200 concurrent active sessions hitting the streaming endpoint; eventual target is 500 but we can stage that.
2) Latency: For customer-facing streaming, we care about token flush latency (i.e., time from model token generation to client receive). Our internal bar is p95 token latency < 120ms; p50 < 60ms would be ideal.
3) Throughput: Typical prompt sizes are ~120 tokens; outbound generation averages 180 tokens per response. Expected sessions have bursts at start of business hour producing ~6k tokens/sec aggregate for the POC window.

Can you confirm whether the 8xA100 Dedicated config you mentioned earlier can sustain 200 concurrent streaming sessions at those token-latency targets? Also please share any benchmark CSVs or logs that show token-level latency distribution.

Best,
Alex
Head of Platform Engineering | FintechCo
alex@fintechco.com

Alex  great details, exactly what we need. Short answers up front, details & artifacts below.

- 8xA100 (Dedicated) is a reasonable starting point and in our benchmarks sustains ~180-220 concurrent streaming sessions at p95 token latency ~100-130ms depending on prompt distribution and decoding strategy. For your target of p95<120ms, we recommend:
  * Use continuous streaming mode with small decode batch size (1-4 tokens) for lowest token flush latency
  * Enable our KV-prefix cache for hot prompts to reduce token compute on repeated patterns
  * Consider quantized model variant (int8) to improve throughput with minimal quality change  we'll validate during POC

- I'm attaching a benchmark CSV that includes token-level latency percentiles from a recent 8xA100 run against a sample workload similar to yours. See the "token_latency_p95" column.

- For throughput: the 8xA100 sustained about 6.5k tokens/sec in our test when optimized; bursts were higher for short-lived prompts. If you expect 6k tokens/sec during the POC window, that aligns with our tested envelope.

Next-step proposal (updated MAP):
1) Share sample production traffic (traces or synthetic workload) by 5/21
2) Rishi to run a 2-day benchmark on a mirrored workload week of 5/25 (we'll provide access to a dedicated test pool)
3) Confirm acceptance criteria: p95 token latency < 120ms, error-rate < 1%, sustained throughput >= 6k tokens/sec for POC
4) Procurement prep: estimate and anticipated commitment for Dedicated during POC

If that sounds right I'll ask Rishi to share an internal benchmark runbook and schedule the workshop.

Thanks 
Marissa

[Attachment: benchmark-results-20260512.csv (csv)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reed <alex@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: FintechCo performance recap & SLO checklist

Alex / Team 

Jumping in with technical detail and a proposed test plan. TL;DR: 8xA100 looks fine as a starting point; we recommend staged tuning during the POC to hit p95<120ms at 200 concurrent streaming sessions.

Key considerations:
- Streaming model behavior: token flush latency is highly sensitive to decode batch size and model variant. For your goals, we'll run with decode batch size = 1 initially.
- Concurrency model: with 200 concurrent sessions we recommend allocating a pool with autoscale headroom for 250 sessions to handle bursts.
- KV/Prefix cache: bring your 10-20 most common prompts (or a percentiles list) to maximize cache hit rate. This reduces compute per token for recurring patterns.
- Metrics to collect during POC: token_latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens_per_sec, active_sessions, model_queue_depth, error_rate per 1m window. We'll instrument with our tracing and provide dashboards.

Planned benchmark runbook:
1) Rishi to provision test pool (8xA100) and load synthetic driver that mirrors your token sizes and session concurrency (2-day run)
2) Collect token-level traces and produce CSV + perf dashboard
3) If p95 > target, iterate: change model variant (int8), tune decode params, add extra nodes or split across 2 pools with smart routing

I've uploaded the runbook and a driver script to the shared Drive and linked it here: https://drive.google.com/fintechco/slo-checklist (see folder "benchmarks"). Also linking the HubSpot deal for tracking: hubspot:HS-55431

Let me know available slots for the technical workshop next week  I have 5/26 (afternoon) or 5/27 (morning) open.

-rishi
